intent: Enable Flow strict typing on the errors tests and inspect-test, and widen the GraphQLError constructor's declared `nodes` type to accept null (the tests pass null as the nodes argument). Inferred from the diff and commit message; the PR body is empty.

findings.title: GraphQLError implementation signature not widened to accept null for `nodes`
findings.suggested_fix: Change the implementation parameter to `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void | null,` so it matches the `declare class` constructor signature at line 25.
findings.why_it_matters: The PR widens only the `declare class` constructor (line 25) to accept null. The exported function that implements it still declares `nodes` without null. The two signatures now disagree, and Flow does not catch it because the declaration is what callers see. Runtime already handles null (`nodes ? [nodes] : undefined`), so behavior is correct; this is type drift between declaration and implementation.
evidence: src/error/GraphQLError.js:25 declare class constructor accepts `| null`
src/error/GraphQLError.js:102-108 runtime treats null like undefined
